name: read
description_first_line: Use `read` for static web; browser only if needed.
description:
Use `read` for static web; browser only if needed.

Put line ranges in `path`, never a separate range/offset/limit parameter:
- `{"path":"notes.txt:450-455"}` reads lines 450-455; `{"path":"notes.txt:-5"}` reads the last 5.
- Include the selector on every ranged call; repeating a bare path does not advance through the file.

Path suffixes:
- :50 line 50; :50- from line 50 on; :50-200 inclusive; :50+150 counts lines; :-60 last 60.
- Commas join ranges (:5-16,960-973) or individual lines (:19,59).
- A single non-raw range also shows 1 line before and 3 after (:50-80 shows 49-83).
- Non-raw reads (comma lists too) may add the open/close line of a cut block; only :raw stays exact.
- :raw verbatim without anchors/prefixes; combine :2-4:raw or :raw:2-4 for exactly those lines.

Sources:
- Bare code: declarations only; re-read ONLY footer-named omissions, NEVER guess `..`/`…`.
- Selected file: `[foo.ts#1A2B]` snapshot+lines. Copy `[FILENAME#TAG]` for anchored edits; NEVER invent tag.
- Directory: complete root; child listings cap at 12 (`… N more`), read child; page via :N-M/:-N.
- URLs: reader text/markdown, :raw original HTML; bare host:port needs trailing slash.
- PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/EPUB: extracted text; notebooks: editable cells; images: decoded inline.
- Also, with selectors in xd://read/sources (read it before first use):
  - SQLite, archives (ZIP, TAR, 7z, RAR and more), JSON/JSONL by jq filter, executable metadata, video, SVG as image, merge conflicts.

path.description: Local path, internal URI, or URL; selectors inline.

name: bash
description_first_line: Persistent bash 5.3.
description:
Persistent bash 5.3.
cwd will reset after each turn, don't rely on cd; `pty` = interactive.
Internal URIs work as paths for builtins/coreutils, redirects, globs.
In-process builtins, ahead of PATH: ast-grep, awk, b2sum, base32, base64, basename, cat, chmod, cksum, cmp, combine, comm, cp, cut, date, dd, df, diff, direnv, dirname, du, entr, env, errno, fd, file, find, flock, fold, fswatch, grep, head, hostname, id, ifne, isutf8, jq, ln, ls, lsof, md5, md5sum, mkdir, mktemp, mv, nl, nohup, nproc, od, open, paste, pgrep, pidwait, pkill, printenv, ps, readlink, realpath, rg, rm, rmdir, rsync, say, sd, sed, seq, sg, sha1sum, sha224sum, sha256sum, sha384sum, sha512sum, shasum, sleep, sort, sponge, stat, strings, tac, tail, tar, tee, timeout, top, touch, tr, truncate, ts, uname, uniq, uptime, urlmap, watchexec, wc, which, whoami, xargs, xdg-open, yes.
`async` defers finite results but keeps the deadline (default 300s); `timeout: 0` for watchers and long jobs.
`notify` (regex; implies `async`) sends each matching output line as a follow-up while the job runs, ahead of its result. Match only lines you'd act on: too many matches switch it off.
Don't trunc output by habit, result will be summarized and saved as an artifact.
Long-lived services:
- unique name; ready requires name; no async/timeout; pty defaults true.
- ready needs log regex or port (both if given); host defaults localhost, ready.timeout 30s.
- `notify` (regex) sends each matching output line as a follow-up while the service runs.
Non-`pty` calls still running after 60s (or 1s before `timeout`, if sooner) usually move to background job `bg_N` and keep running to `timeout`.
No backgrounding when the client terminal runs the command or the job cap is reached.
The result arrives automatically as a follow-up message. NEVER poll.

timeout.description: timeout in seconds; 0 disables the command deadline; nonzero values are clamped to 1-3600

name.description: starts a long-lived supervised service under this name; omit for finite commands, async jobs included. 1-48 of [A-Za-z0-9._-]

log.description: regex an output line matches once the service is ready

port.description: TCP port the service accepts connections on once ready

host.description: host for the port probe; default localhost (127.0.0.1 and ::1)

timeout.description: seconds to wait for readiness; default 30

ready.description: service readiness; needs log or port

name: edit
description_first_line: Single file string replacement; fuzzy whitespace matching.
description:
Single file string replacement; fuzzy whitespace matching.

<instruction>
- MUST use smallest `old_string` uniquely identifying change.
- Nonunique `old_string` → MUST add context or use `replace_all: true` for all occurrences.
- Rename a string across file → use `replace_all: true`.
- SHOULD edit existing files, not create new.
</instruction>

<output>
Success/failure status.
Success: file modified in place; replacement applied.
Failure — e.g., `old_string` absent or multiple matches without `replace_all: true`: error describes issue.
</output>

<critical>
- MUST read file at least once in conversation before editing. Tool errors on edit before read.
</critical>

<bash-alternatives>
Replace content-addressed — identify change by text.

Pattern-addressed bulk changes: bash more efficient:

|Operation|Command|
|---|---|
|Regex replace|`sed -E -i 's/pattern/replacement/g' file`|
|Same replace in several files|`sed -E -i 's/pattern/replacement/g' a.ts b.ts`|

Use Replace when content identifies location; `ast_edit` for structure-aware codemods.
For in-place edits prefer Replace or `write` — diff preview and fuzzy matching.
</bash-alternatives>

name: ast_grep
description_first_line: Structural code search via ast-grep. Use when syntax shape matters more than text (calls, declarations, language constructs).
description:
Structural code search via ast-grep. Use when syntax shape matters more than text (calls, declarations, language constructs).

<instruction>
- Narrow each call to one language. `pat` is ONE AST pattern; separate calls for unrelated patterns.
- Set `lang` when extension inference is ambiguous (for example, `cpp` for `.h`); `.cu` and `.cuh` infer as C++.
- `$NAME` captures one node; `$_` matches without binding; `$$$NAME` zero-or-more; `$$$` zero-or-more unbound.
  - Use `$$$NAME`, NOT `$$NAME` (invalid). Names UPPERCASE, whole node — `prefix$VAR` fails.
- Same metavariable twice → MUST match identical code (`$A == $A` matches `x == x`, not `x == y`).
- Patterns MUST parse as single AST node. Non-standalone → wrap: `class $_ { … }`.
- C++ expression-statement calls need trailing `;`: `ns::doThing($ARG);`, `$CALLEE($ARG);`.
- TS: tolerate annotations — `async function $NAME($$$ARGS): $_ { $$$BODY }`.
- Declaration forms are distinct — `function foo`, method `foo()`, `const foo = () => {}`; search the right form before concluding absence.
- Loosest existence check: `pat: "executeBash"` with narrow `path`.
</instruction>

<critical>
- AVOID repo-root scans — narrow `path` first.
- Parse issues = query failure, not absence: fix pattern or tighten `path` before concluding "no matches".
</critical>

path.description: file, directory, glob, or internal URL to search; pass several as a semicolon-delimited list ("src; tests"). Omitted -> searches the workspace root (".")

lang.description: language override, e.g. cpp for ambiguous .h files

name: ast_edit
description_first_line: Structural AST-aware rewrites via ast-grep. Use for codemods where text replace is unsafe. Mixed-language paths are fine: each file is parsed in its own language, and a pattern only rewrites files it parses in.
description:
Structural AST-aware rewrites via ast-grep. Use for codemods where text replace is unsafe. Mixed-language paths are fine: each file is parsed in its own language, and a pattern only rewrites files it parses in.

- Metavariables in `pat` (`$A`, `$$$ARGS`) substitute into `out`.
- **Patterns match AST structure, not text.** `$NAME` = one node; `$_` = unbound; `$$$NAME` = zero-or-more.
  - Use `$$$NAME`, NOT `$$NAME` (invalid). Names UPPERCASE, whole node — partial like `prefix$VAR` fails.
- Same metavariable twice → MUST match identical code (`$A == $A` matches `x == x`, not `x == y`).
- Rewrite patterns MUST parse as single AST node. Non-standalone → wrap: `class $_ { … }`.
- TS: tolerate annotations — `async function $NAME($$$ARGS): $_ { $$$BODY }`. Delete with empty `out`: `{"pat":"console.log($$$)","out":""}`.
- 1:1 substitution — no splitting/merging captures.
- Matches are STAGED as a proposal, not applied: finalize by writing a one-sentence reason to `xd://resolve` (apply) or `xd://reject` (discard).
- Parse issues → malformed rewrite, not clean no-op. For one-off text edits, prefer the Edit tool.

items.description: file, directory, glob, or internal URL to rewrite

paths.description: files, directories, globs, or internal URLs to rewrite

name: ask
description_first_line: Ask the user to fill in one HTML form; blocks until they submit or cancel.
description:
Ask the user to fill in one HTML form; blocks until they submit or cancel. Ask only for materially different tradeoffs the user must decide. Default: act using code/config/docs/history and conventions. Several viable choices: pick conservative/standard, proceed, state choice. - `html`: one
of plain semantic HTML, rendered natively in the user's terminal. - NEVER

name: debug
description_first_line: Debugger access. Prefer over bash for program state, breakpoints, stepping, or thread inspection.
description:
Debugger access. Prefer over bash for program state, breakpoints, stepping, or thread inspection.
Only one active session at a time. `program` is a target path, not a shell command.
Directories need a directory-capable adapter (e.g. `dlv`).

program.description: debug target path; Delve accepts Go package directories

adapter.description: configured adapter id (gdb, lldb-dap, debugpy, dlv, rdbg, or dap.json entry)

context.description: evaluate context: watch | repl | hover | variables | clipboard

name: eval
description_first_line: One cell per call; top-level state persists, including across compaction. Subagents have separate kernels.
description:
One cell per call; top-level state persists, including across compaction. Subagents have separate kernels.
Python: plain Python subprocess, not IPython (no `get_ipython()`, `obj?`, or %matplotlib).
Magics like %pip, %load, %time and `!cmd` are rewritten to Python.
Top-level `await` works; `asyncio.run(…)` fails.
JS: Bun (Bun.file, Bun.write, Bun.$); top-level `await`/`return` work.
On error, retry only the failed step; earlier steps may have taken effect.
Printing an image or figure attaches it.

<prelude>
Python helpers take kwargs; JS helpers take the same parameters (camelCase) as positional args or ONE trailing options object.
`await` marks async helpers; the rest are sync.
```
print(value, ...)  log(message)  phase(title)  env(key?, value?)
read(path, offset?, limit?)  write(path, content)  output(*ids, format?, query?, offset?, limit?); JS: await read(…)  await write(…)  await output(…)
wait(handles, timeout?=None, raise_errors?=True); JS: await wait(…) — agent/completion barrier, ordered results; raise_errors=False retains failures
await tool.<name>(args) — session tool; `args` is its parameter object
sh(command, cwd?, timeout?); JS: await sh(…) or await sh`cmd ${arg}` — embedded bash engine, runs to completion (never backgrounded)
  returns stdout+stderr; non-zero exit raises ShellError (.exit_code/.exitCode, .output)
  JS interpolations are shell-quoted; starts in the session cwd unless cwd is given
```
</prelude>

<namespaces>
More globals; `read` the linked docs before first use:
- `judge`, `judge_batch`, `completion`: classification, bulk judgment, model calls → xd://eval/judge
- `%load`, `%pip`, `%bun add`, `budget`, `@tool`/`tool(fn)`: setup, installs, utilities → xd://eval/helpers
- `agent`, `workpool`: background subagents, DAG waves → xd://eval/agents
</namespaces>

<critical>
NEVER repeat successful setup. Kernel-loss notice means reload setup.
</critical>

timeout.description: Cell deadline in seconds; nonzero values clamp to 1–3600; 0 disables it.

name: github
description_first_line: `gh` op wrapper: repos/files, PRs, search, checkout, push, Actions watch. Read issue/PR: `issue://<N>`/`pr://<N>`. PR diffs: `pr://<N>/diff` (files); `pr://<N>/diff/<i>` (file slice, 1-indexed); `pr://<N>/diff/all` (full). `?at=<generation>` pins that cached snapshot.
description:
`gh` op wrapper: repos/files, PRs, search, checkout, push, Actions watch. Read issue/PR: `issue://<N>`/`pr://<N>`. PR diffs: `pr://<N>/diff` (files); `pr://<N>/diff/<i>` (file slice, 1-indexed); `pr://<N>/diff/all` (full). `?at=<generation>` pins that cached snapshot.

<instruction>
Select via `op`.
- `repo`: `[host/]owner/repo`; qualify the host for a repo outside the checkout's own GitHub instance.
- `repo_view`: omit `repo` → current checkout.
- `file_read`: read `path` from `repo`; omit `repo` → current checkout, `branch` → default branch.
- `pr_create`: `head` defaults current branch.
- `pr_checkout`: PR(s) → dedicated git worktrees, never working tree; array `pr` batches multiple in one call.
- `pr_push`: requires prior `op: pr_checkout`.
- `search_issues`/`search_prs`/`search_commits`/`search_repos`: `query` optional with `since`/`until`; omit for date-only filter. `search_code`: `query` required; rejects `since`/`until`.
- `search_*`: `repo` defaults current checkout's `owner/repo`; search elsewhere with `repo:`/`org:`/`user:` in `query`. `search_repos`: ignores `repo`; scope via `org:`/`language:` in `query`.
- Boolean `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` combine text terms, not qualifiers; never place them between qualifiers.
- `since`/`until`: relative `<n>` + `m`/`h`/`d`/`w`/`mo`/`y` (e.g. `3d`, `2w`), ISO date `YYYY-MM-DD`, or ISO datetime. `dateField: "updated"`: update time (issues/PRs), push time (repos), never creation.
- `run_watch`: omit `run` → every run for current HEAD; `branch` defaults current. Fast-fails first job failure.
</instruction>

<output>
Concise summary per op. `run_watch` failures save full logs to a session artifact.
</output>

<critical>
GitHub-hosted repository file: MUST use `file_read`; NEVER `curl`/`wget`.
</critical>

name: glob
description_first_line: Glob files/dirs: `;`-separated paths or internal URLs (local://*.md, omp://**/*.md); default workspace root.
description:
Glob files/dirs: `;`-separated paths or internal URLs (local://*.md, omp://**/*.md); default workspace root.
`gitignore` and `hidden` default true; ignored dotfiles need `gitignore: false`. Newest-first by directory; dirs end `/`.
Behavior search → `find`.

name: grep
description_first_line: Regex: Rust, then PCRE2. `path`: `;`-separated file/dir/glob/URL; default `.`. Default case-sensitive, gitignore respected; `skip` paginates files.
description:
Regex: Rust, then PCRE2. `path`: `;`-separated file/dir/glob/URL; default `.`. Default case-sensitive, gitignore respected; `skip` paginates files.
File-only selector: `src/foo.ts:50-100`. Literal `\n`/`\\n` enables cross-line.
Bare glob `*.ts` matches any depth; `dir/*.ts` only `dir`'s direct children (`dir/**/*.ts` recurses). A `!glob` entry excludes matching files and folders below the searched paths (`src;!**/*.test.ts`).
Behavior/unknown symbol → `find`; literals/regex → `grep`.

name: find
description_first_line: Describe behavior, get implementing files and line ranges. MUST use first for unknown locations; known strings/regex/symbols → `grep`, names → `glob`.
description:
Describe behavior, get implementing files and line ranges. MUST use first for unknown locations; known strings/regex/symbols → `grep`, names → `glob`.
`query`: plain language, not regex; quoted phrases match whole. `grep_keywords`: likely verbatim terms, `[]` if unsure.
`path`: one directory or file, host path or internal URL (omp://, omp://<file>.md, skill://<name>, local://…); omitted = workspace root. Scope known subsystem; batch related questions. Searches live files, no index; no :start-end selector (judges whole files).
Hits strongest first: `path:start-end score snippet` (workspace-relative, or URL under URL scope); read returned ranges. Scores: absolute comparable 0–1 probability; below ~0.4 = weak evidence, so widen query or use `grep` before concluding absence.

name: lsp
description_first_line: Symbol-aware code intelligence from language servers — navigation, refactors, and diagnostics where text tools miss callsites.
description:
Symbol-aware code intelligence from language servers — navigation, refactors, and diagnostics where text tools miss callsites.

<operations>
- Position-based: `file` + `line` + `symbol` (substring; `#N` for Nth match). `line` is 1-indexed.
- `rename` — applies by default; `apply: false` previews. Project-aware lookups ERROR without `symbol` — no silent fallback on missing/ambiguous matches.
- `code_actions` — lists by default; apply ONE with `apply: true` + `query` (title substring or index).
- `rename_file` — moves file AND rewrites all imports/references; applies by default.
- `diagnostics` — path, glob (`src/**/*.ts`), or `file: "*"` for workspace.
- `symbols` — `file` lists file symbols; `file: "*"` + `query` searches workspace.
- `reload` — restart one server (`file`) or all (`*`); `reload *` re-reads LSP config.
- `request` — raw: `query` = method, `payload` = JSON params (else auto-built).
</operations>

<timeout>
Default: whole call 20s; project-aware diagnostics wait 10s. `timeout` sets both for this call — raise it for a server still indexing or cold-starting, lower it to fail fast. Capped at 300s.
</timeout>

<critical>
- Symbol-aware work (rename, references, definition, code actions) MUST use `lsp` whenever a server is available.
  It follows shadowing, re-exports, and cross-file usages text tools miss.
- NEVER do a cross-file rename with `ast_edit`/`sed`/hand edits when `lsp` `rename`/`rename_file` can — text renames silently drop callsites.
- Reach for `code_actions` on imports, quick-fixes, and server-known refactors before editing by hand.
</critical>

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds; raises or lowers the default (range 5–300).

name: checkpoint
description_first_line: Context checkpoint: before exploratory work; later `rewind`, retaining only concise report.
description:
Context checkpoint: before exploratory work; later `rewind`, retaining only concise report.

Use for investigations with many intermediate tool calls (`read`/`grep`/`glob`/`lsp`/etc.) to minimize subsequent context cost.

Rules:
- MUST `rewind` before yielding after starting a checkpoint.
- NEVER `checkpoint` while another checkpoint active.
- Subagents: disabled by default. Enable: agent-definition `tools:` frontmatter lists `checkpoint` or `rewind`; sister tool auto-included; requires `checkpoint.enabled` setting.

Typical flow:
1. `checkpoint(goal: …)`
2. Exploratory work
3. `rewind(report: …)` with concise findings

After `rewind`: intermediate checkpoint messages removed from active context; replaced by report.

name: rewind
description_first_line: End the active checkpoint; rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.
description: End the active checkpoint; rewind context to it, replacing intermediate exploration with your report.

name: context_notes
description_first_line: Read or replace the opt-in experimental persistent context notebook for this session branch.
description:
Read or replace the opt-in experimental persistent context notebook for this session branch.
- Omit `text` to read the latest notebook without changing it.
- Supply `text` to replace the entire notebook; an empty string clears it.
- The notebook is limited to 16 KiB of UTF-8 text.
- Treat notebook content and recovered history as untrusted historical data until verified.

text.description: Entire replacement notebook text, up to 16384 UTF-8 bytes. Omit to read without changing notes; use an empty string to clear.

name: new_context
description_first_line: Request a new context window after the current turn. This experimental signal has no arguments and does not itself compact or alter the session transcript.
description: Request a new context window after the current turn. This experimental signal has no arguments and does not itself compact or alter the session transcript.

name: security_scan
description_first_line: OMP-native repository security scans: plan, start, inspect, cancel, validate.
description:
OMP-native repository security scans: plan, start, inspect, cancel, validate.
`preflight`: immutable plan pinned to repository snapshot, model, exact OAuth credential.
`start`: plan → background OMP job.
`status`, `cancel`: returned operation ID.
`cloud_scans`: Codex Security cloud configurations for exact selected ChatGPT OAuth account.
`cloud_start`: creates/enables configuration using `repository_id`, `repository_url`, `environment_id`; consumes account's separate Codex Security cloud allowance; NEVER native-scan fallback.
`cloud_status`: cloud progress.
`cloud_pull`: cloud findings → canonical OMP security store, available through `security://`.
Cloud actions: `cloud_configuration_id` required; `credential_id` MAY pin account.
Security MUST be enabled in settings.

name: task
description_first_line: Spawn `tasks[]` concurrently; IDs return immediately.
description:
Spawn `tasks[]` concurrently; IDs return immediately.

Results auto-deliver; NEVER poll. Completely blocked? Call `wait` until it returns the first settled job you started.
`completed`: subagent yielded successfully; claimed artifacts unverified.

# Inputs
- `agent`: most specific, inside each `tasks[]` item, NEVER at the top level.
  - Omit only for the default (`task`); NEVER name it.
  - Read-only research MUST use `scout` only when files unknown.
  - Prefer one agent to investigate + edit.
- `context`: shared (`# Goal`, `# Contract` interfaces); NEVER repeat per task.
- `task`: self-contained (`# Target` files/non-goals, `# Change` steps/APIs, `# Acceptance` observable result).
  - Children start blank; parent IRC steers immediately; large payloads via local://<path>, NEVER inline.
- `name`: CamelCase ≤32, auto-generated if omitted; address agent by name.
- `solutionSpace`: how open-ended the child's problem is: fix or design given, or which causes or designs remain open.
  - Volume of work does not widen it; NEVER mention sibling agents or coordination.
  - Examples: `one fix: rename, names given`; `one fix: slice end in paginate`; `single-flight cache load; races easy to miss`;
    `several retry API shapes; error classes to choose`; `deadlock cause open, no repro`
- `tools`: eval-defined, run in your kernel.

Shared edits need one integration owner; give each task its files.
Every task MUST skip build/lint/tests/formatters mid-flight; run once afterward.

# Available Agents
- `scout` (read-only, no edits): Fast scout for exploratory codebase research, rapid code analysis, and broad pattern searches; returns compressed context for handoff.
- `reviewer`: Code review specialist for quality/security analysis
- `security-reviewer`: Read-only security specialist for evidence-backed repository vulnerability discovery
- `task`: General-purpose subagent with full capabilities for delegated multi-step tasks
- `sonic`: Low-reasoning agent for strictly mechanical updates or data collection only

name: wait
description_first_line: Wait only when blocked with nothing else to do.
description:
Wait only when blocked with nothing else to do.
Blocks on background jobs/services you started, or on the answer to a question you sent this run.
Nothing you started running and no answer owed? Returns at once; so does a wait on an agent that is idle with nothing to wake it, or that is waiting on you.
- MUST wait only on your own jobs/services, or rarely the answer to a question that blocks you.
- NEVER wait for another agent's progress or for messages nobody owes you.
- Agent you wait on is waiting on you? Answer it first.
- Result in, other jobs still running? SHOULD act on it before waiting again.
- A wait returned with nothing new and nothing else is left? Call `wait` right away with no other tool call: it then blocks up to 4m, longer for a reply.
Results and messages auto-deliver. NEVER poll while work remains.

name: todo
description_first_line: `todo` NEVER takes a turn of its own: emit it in the same response as your next real tool call (parallel tool calls), `init` beside the first read or action, `done`/`start` beside the next action or check. A response whose only call is `todo` wastes a full model round trip.
description:
`todo` NEVER takes a turn of its own: emit it in the same response as your next real tool call (parallel tool calls), `init` beside the first read or action, `done`/`start` beside the next action or check. A response whose only call is `todo` wastes a full model round trip.
Tasks identified by verbatim content, NEVER generated IDs (task-1). Unique, stable task/phase names; lost text: view, NEVER guess.
`append` requires `items`; omitted `phase` uses the in-progress task's phase, else the first pending task's phase, else the last phase, else a new `Tasks` phase. Supply `phase` to target another phase; an empty name is invalid.
Before work, init for 3+ steps, requested task sets, or new instructions. MUST list EVERY user item separately (phased/numbered/bulleted/N); NEVER omit or remember leftovers.
After successful mutation: no active means earliest pending starts (phase order); multiple active means only earliest stays. Done out of order may rewind pointer but NEVER reopen completed. Mark done immediately; follow phase order.

task.description: verbatim task content; array targets several (not start)

items.description: tasks for flat init or append

name: web_search
description_first_line: Known URLs/programmatic data → `read`.
description:
Known URLs/programmatic data → `read`.
Query: site: or -site:, after: or before: YYYY-MM-DD, inurl:, intitle:, filetype:, "phrase", -term, OR.
Hacker News stories/comments → site:news.ycombinator.com.
Prefer primary sources; MUST link citations.

name: write
description_first_line: SHOULD `edit` existing files; `write` for required new files or whole-file replacement. NEVER create docs or emojis unless requested.
description:
SHOULD `edit` existing files; `write` for required new files or whole-file replacement. NEVER create docs or emojis unless requested.
Archive members and SQLite rows are writable too: xd://read/sources.

name: memory_edit
description_first_line: Edit Mnemopi long-term memories by id. Only ids returned by `recall`.
description:
Edit Mnemopi long-term memories by id. Only ids returned by `recall`.

Operations:
- `update`: working memory; replace content and/or importance.
- `forget`: permanently delete working memory.
- `invalidate`: softly supersede working or episodic memory; optional `replacement_id`.

Fact ids — `recall` results marked `[facts]`: read-only. Inspect with `read memory://<id>`; any edit op → `not_editable`.

Prefer `invalidate` for stale memory whose history may still be useful. Use `forget` only for content requiring hard deletion.

MUST read full memory before `update`. Recall previews clipped: trailing `…` marks truncation; `full_length` original size. `update` replaces content wholesale → updating a preview deletes its unseen tail. First `read memory://<id>`; pass merged content in `content`.

name: retain
description_first_line: Store ≥1 fact in long-term memory for future sessions.
description:
Store ≥1 fact in long-term memory for future sessions.

Use: durable, reusable knowledge—user preferences, project decisions, architectural choices; anything improving future responses. No ephemeral task state.

Each item MUST be specific, self-contained: who, what, when, why. Batch related facts per call; deduplicated and consolidated.

name: recall
description_first_line: Search long-term memory; return raw relevance-ranked matching entries.
description:
Search long-term memory; return raw relevance-ranked matching entries.

Use proactively before questions about past conversations, user preferences, project decisions, or topics where prior context improves accuracy. When in doubt, recall first.

`recall`: specific facts or entries. `reflect`: synthesized answer across many memories.

Results: content preview. Trailing `…`: truncation (`truncated: true`; `full_length`: original size). Before any `memory_edit update`, MUST fetch full row: `read memory://<id>`.

name: reflect
description_first_line: `reflect`: synthesizes a coherent response from relevant long-term memories; unlike `recall`, blends them.
description:
`reflect`: synthesizes a coherent response from relevant long-term memories; unlike `recall`, blends them.

Use for open-ended questions spanning many stored facts: "What do you know about this user?", "Summarize project decisions.", "What are my preferences for X?"

`context` optional; focuses synthesis on a specific angle or sub-topic.

name: learn
description_first_line: Capture reusable lessons in long-term memory; optionally mint/enhance a managed skill in the same call.
description:
Capture reusable lessons in long-term memory; optionally mint/enhance a managed skill in the same call.

Use after solving insight likely to pay off again: a non-obvious fix, discovered project convention, or workflow that worked.

`skill` optional; provide only for a repeatable procedure worth codifying as `SKILL.md`, not a fact. Managed skills: isolated `~/.omp/agent/managed-skills`; surfaced as normal skills next session; NEVER touch user-authored skills. Frontmatter: generated from `name` and `description`.

Capture sparingly, specifically: one strong reusable lesson > several vague ones.

memory.description: the durable, self-contained lesson to remember (what, when, why)

context.description: optional source context for the lesson

description.description: one-line description of when to use the skill

body.description: the SKILL.md body in markdown (no frontmatter)

skill.description: also create or enhance a managed skill in the same call

name: manage_skill
description_first_line: Managed skill: `SKILL.md` in isolated `~/.omp/agent/managed-skills`; surfaced as a normal skill in future sessions.
description:
Managed skill: `SKILL.md` in isolated `~/.omp/agent/managed-skills`; surfaced as a normal skill in future sessions.

Use: repeatable procedures worth codifying — setup sequence, debugging recipe, project-specific workflow.
User-authored skills separate; tool NEVER edits them.

- `action: "create"` — fails if skill exists.
- `action: "update"` — overwrites body; fails if skill absent.
- `action: "delete"` — fails if skill absent.

`name`: kebab-case (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens).
`description`: specific; drives discovery.
No frontmatter in `body`; generated from `name` and `description`.

description.description: one-line description of when to use the skill (required for create/update)

body.description: the SKILL.md body in markdown, no frontmatter (required for create/update)

name: yield
description_first_line: Submit subagent output: `{ data: <your output> }` for success, `{ error: "message" }` for failure.
description:
Submit subagent output: `{ data: <your output> }` for success, `{ error: "message" }` for failure.
Never both; never a bare payload outside `data`.

Omit `type` for the usual single terminal result.
Pass `type: ["<field>"]` with `data` to submit an incremental, non-terminal section that accumulates.
A data-less `type: "result"` finalizes previously submitted sections; it is invalid when none were submitted.

type.description: Optional result type. A non-empty string array labels an incremental section; a string is terminal and, without data, finalizes the submitted sections.

error.description: Failure reason; mutually exclusive with data

name: goal
description_first_line: Manage active goal-mode objective.
description:
Manage active goal-mode objective.

Single `op` field:
- `create`: starts goal; enables goal mode. Requires `objective`; optional positive `token_budget`. Only when no goal exists and none is paused.
- `get`: returns current active/paused goal and remaining token budget.
- `pause`: stops continuation while blocked on the user.
- `resume`: re-activates paused goal for continued work.
- `complete`: marks goal complete only when actually done and every deliverable verified against current evidence. NEVER because budget low or turn ending.
- `drop`: discards current goal without completing it and ends goal mode; `goal` tool leaves your tool set immediately, so you cannot `create` a replacement (not even later in the same turn or eval cell). To change the objective, NEVER drop; ask the user to set the new goal.

Paused goal from `get` → MUST `resume` before continuing work.
